public_rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and no verified event satisfies the early-resolution rule. Selected GPU underutilization predates the forecast and does not establish a market-wide economic surplus. A purchaser's reported shortage provides countervailing context but cannot rule out eventual overbuilding.
limitations: Technical utilization is not the same measure as paid occupancy or economic demand.
The late-recognition clause requires evidence about investment decisions as well as capacity.
The indefinite horizon prevents a conclusive negative outcome from ordinary continued non-occurrence.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI capacity will eventually come online at a scale the compute market can't support, and this won't be obvious until too late.

statement.excerpt: Capacity will, eventually, come online at a scale that the market for AI compute cannot support, and it won’t be obvious until it’s way, way too late.

from_speaker: at a scale that the market for AI compute cannot support
it won’t be obvious until it’s way, way too late
our_interpretation: The plain reading is a substantial, widespread surplus of operating AI compute capacity relative to economically sustainable demand.
The second clause means that the surplus becomes broadly recognized after substantial investment commitments can no longer be avoided.
A failed project, temporary idle capacity, or low chip utilization caused by technical inefficiency does not alone establish a market-wide surplus.
criteria.support_condition: Sustained evidence across a representative share of operating AI compute capacity shows insufficient economic demand, corroborated by distressed pricing or stranded investment, with recognition following substantial irreversible commitments.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Finite evidence of healthy demand cannot conclusively disprove an unrestricted eventual forecast. Evidence that an identified surplus was recognized before avoidable commitments were made would count against the late-recognition component.
